title: Closing Cost Credit Holdings per Customer and the Calendar-Year Reservation Limit
content:
**Larkspur Closing Cost Credit — Credit Program Policy, holdings per customer**

1. A customer may hold Closing Cost Credits on several loan files over time. There is no limit on the number of credits one customer may hold.
2. On any one loan file, the combination rules for credits on the same loan file apply.
3. Each program may be reserved by one customer at most the program's number of reservations per customer per calendar year. The count covers every credit of the same customer and the same program whose reservation date falls in the calendar year of the reservation date, whatever that credit's status.

### The same clause, piece by piece

| Question | Answer under the clause |
|---|---|
| Is there a ceiling on credits per customer across all files? | No; the number is unlimited. |
| What is counted against the yearly limit? | Credits of the same customer and the same program reserved in the same calendar year. |
| Does an expired, revoked or forfeited credit still count? | Yes; the count takes every status. |
| Does a credit of another program count? | No; the count is per program. |

### Worked illustration (hypothetical)

Take a program whose limit is one reservation per customer per calendar year.

- A customer reserved that program on 10 February of one year, and the credit later expired. A second reservation of the same program on 1 September of the same year would be a second reservation in that calendar year: the count already stands at one, so the limit is reached.
- A reservation of the same program on 4 January of the following year falls in a new calendar year, where the count starts again from the credits reserved in that year.
- A reservation of a different program on 1 September of the first year is counted under that other program only.
